Input Statement: If A is an n×n matrix with strictly positive entries, then there exists a simple, strictly maximal, positive eigenvalue r with a strictly positive eigenvector.

Notes: This hard negative from Gemini takes the conclusion that the dominant eigenvalue of a positive matrix will be the largest eigenvalue and reverses it to being the smallest eigenvalue. Statements should be mathematically different.

Notes: This hard negative from Qwen tries to change the conclusion from eigenvalues of A to eigenvalues of A^T, but because eigenvalues are preserved under transpose, these statements are not mathematically distinct.
